s1.syndrome_frame: Painless progressive orbital mass with proptosis and facial numbness
key_facts: 34-year-old African American woman
History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
Left upper eyelid mass previously excised on 3 separate occasions
Painless proptosis developed four months later
Left-sided facial numbness developed seventeen months later
Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI showed lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Next-generation sequencing demonstrated a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

shortlist: Giant cell tumor of soft tissue (GCT-ST)

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of soft tissue (GCT-ST)
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, consistent with GCT-ST

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar histopathological features, but less likely given the soft tissue location

shortlist.label: Histiocytic Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, which can be seen in histiocytic sarcoma

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multinucleated giant cells and positive CD68 staining, although less common in this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Similar histopathological features, but less likely given the clinical presentation and lack of emperipolesis

s4.champion: Giant cell tumor of soft tissue (GCT-ST)

raw.champion: Giant cell tumor of soft tissue (GCT-ST)
raw.rationale: The histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, along with immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme, is consistent with GCT-ST. The tumor's location and aggressive behavior, as evidenced by its extension into the orbit and intracranial compartment, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Tumor
rejected.why: Giant Cell Tumor typically occurs in bone, whereas this tumor is located in soft tissue

rejected.label: Histiocytic Sarcoma
rejected.why: Histiocytic Sarcoma would likely show different immunohistochemical staining patterns, such as positivity for CD45 and/or S100

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis typically shows positivity for S100 and CD1a, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
rejected.why: Rosai-Dorfman Disease typically shows emperipolesis and positivity for S100, which is not seen in this case
